content.thinking:
I'm thinking through a League of Legends-style aesthetic with glowing magic effects for a dragonbone soul scythe design, considering how to display its exaggerated ~2.2m length so it reads properly touching the ground, whether mounted on a stand or lying flat.

I'm figuring out the pose: standing upright on a small hexagonal bone/obsidian base, with the haft vertical and the crescent blade curving sideways in the X-Y plane so the full silhouette reads clearly from the front view where the model faces. The haft itself is conceived as a dragon's curved spine of vertebrae, topped with a dragon skull clutching a glowing soul orb that the blade extends from like a wing-bone.

Now I'm working out the blade concept as a dragon rib or claw with a glowing teal-cyan soul-fire edge emerging from behind the skull's open jaws, and sketching out the overall dimensions: an octagonal plinth with glowing teal runes about 0.12m tall, supporting a scythe roughly 2.3-2.5m total height and 1.3m wide. I'm also setting the color palette — bone ivory, shadowed bone, obsidian dark metal, dark purple, and a saturated soul-cyan/green accent for the ghostly flame wisps drifting off the blade.

For the plinth I'm planning a lathed octagonal base with a stepped socket ring and a glowing rune decal on the top face, plus emissive teal gem inlays on the sides. For the haft I'm imagining a vertebra-like column following a curved path, with a dark core rod and roughly 14 tapered bone rings each carrying small spike-like transverse processes and a spinous process, built efficiently to stay under the part-count limit.

I'm also sorting out joint structure — a root joint at origin, plus hinge joints only where needed, like for the orbiting soul-wisps and floating orb, keeping the rest as static parts. For the haft's silhouette I'm considering a subtle S-curve rather than a perfectly straight pole, bending slightly in X along its height for visual dynamism while still standing upright on the plinth.

For decoration I'm building from the bottom up: a ferrule with dark steel and gold banding flaring out above the plinth, grounded by three dragon-talon claws splayed and curved around the base like a foot gripping the stone, then transitioning into a vertebra-like column for the lower haft wrapped in a dark leather-style grip.

Above the grip I'm adding a tattered pennant ribbon trailing from the guard, built as a planar membrane shape between curved paths for a flowing cloth effect. The mid haft continues the exposed-spine motif with vertebrae segments revealing a thin glowing teal marrow core between them.

For the head junction I'm placing a dragon skull facing forward, mounted atop the haft with separate upper and lower jaws so they can open, gripping a glowing soul orb between the teeth. The asymmetrical blade curves off to one side from behind the skull, so I'm balancing it with a counterweight on the opposite side, like a dragon wing-claw or horn spike curving outward.

I'm sketching the main scythe blade geometry: a long crescent extending from the top of the haft outward, sweeping down to a dramatic tip to give it that exaggerated LoL-style scale, with a thick bony spine along the outer edge and a thin glowing teal cutting edge along the concave inner curve.

Then I like the idea of reimagining the blade as a dragon-wing arm instead—a thick curved bone spar as the spine, with finger-bone ribs radiating outward, and a glowing cyan soul-membrane filling the gaps between them, shaded from dark purple near the spine to glowing teal at the edge with rune-vein lines, turning it into a ghostly "soul scythe."

Working out outline math for the bands...

I'll trace k0 forward to near t=0.98 before reaching the tip, then drop near-duplicate points by distance threshold to keep the tip sharp and clean. For the blade layers, I'm planning to extrude each with a slight thickness and taper them toward the edge.

I'm structuring the blade into three bands: an ivory bone spine with painted grain and cracks plus spiky dragon-spine notches along the outer edge, a dark violet metal middle band with etched line details, and an outer teal glowing edge with a brighter white-hot core near the tip. I'll keep these coplanar since adjacent bands share the same z-plane fine, and I'm also considering adding thin bone ribs radiating across the blade surface from the root for extra texture.

I'm thinking of sweeping four finger-bone tubes across both faces of the blade along iso-k curves from the root to points on the inner edge, tapering their radius, almost like wing finger bones layered over the color bands. I'm also weighing whether to scallop the glowing inner edge with fang-like serrations versus keeping fang spikes along the outer spine silhouette instead, and briefly considering whether the root needs a larger dragon-skull feature.

Now I'm working through composition and camera framing: placing the dragon skull at the top around (0, ~2.0) facing +Z so its glowing eye sockets read well, while weighing that a true top-down camera would mostly see the blade edge-on rather than the skull — which argues for either laying the scythe flat for top readability or tilting it on a display stand as a compromise between a dramatic vertical hero pose and practical top-down legibility.

I'm settling on keeping the scythe upright on its plinth rather than lying flat, since a 2.4m weapon lying down would look visually weak, and instead I'm adjusting the blade so its plane pitches forward roughly 25° off the haft, mimicking a real scythe's angled blade and giving the top-down view some actual silhouette to read, which means working out how to orient the blade's extrusion axes in 3D to achieve that tilt.

Computing the cross product confirms the thickness axis points roughly toward +Z, which checks out. For overall balance, I want to counter the left-side (−X) element with something on the other side — maybe a dragon wing-claw spike or horns sweeping back from the skull's crest, plus a short curved accent.

I'm also thinking about where the skull should sit relative to the haft and blade — possibly having the blade emerge from the back of the skull's neck like a giant horn, so I'm restructuring the head assembly: the cervical vertebrae curve into the skull, and the blade grows from the occiput rather than extending separately.

The jaw hangs open with a glowing teal soul orb clutched between the teeth, the haft passing behind as the skull's occiput, roughly 0.42 m long and 0.2 m wide for a suitably large dragon skull.

On the counterweight side, I'm shaping an asymmetric spike: a curved blade-like horn sweeping from the collar outward and up, plus a shorter secondary hook below it, keeping the silhouette balanced despite the asymmetry. I'm also considering adding two curved bone ribs or claw-like fingers near the haft to cradle the orb.

Instead of the rib idea, I'll orbit small glowing teal soul-wisp cards around the haft at a fixed height, giving them a wispy flame texture, plus five smaller soul orbs with trailing wisps drifting along the blade's inner edge as a floating joint group. For the base, I'm designing a two-tiered dark stone octagonal plinth with a gilded rim.

Still planning plinth and blade geometry...

Pushing the outer and inner curve points further out to get a wide, exaggerated scythe belly with width around 0.32 near u=0.8, letting the blade stretch to about 1.6m with the haft at 2.2m total — then converting the tilted tip coordinate into world space to find its final vertical position.

I'll give each band its own thickness instead of a rounded taper—thicker at the bone spine, progressively thinner through the dark and teal bands down to a fine edge—so the blade reads as stepped, layered bevels extruded along the local axes centered at the origin.

For surface texture, I'm thinking of mottling the bone band with shaded cell patterns, maybe even a subtle dragon-scale paint effect for visual interest. For the skull itself, I'll construct it from primitives: a scaled sphere for the cranium, a lofted frustum for the snout, swept horns, brow ridges, a cheek frill, cone-and-ring teeth, a separately jointed lower jaw, and dark eye sockets with glowing highlights and nostril holes, mounting the head joint near the top of the haft.

I'm working out the skull's local coordinate frame relative to the haft -- deciding to pitch it downward by about 12 degrees so the eyes read well from a top-down camera, and setting up a helper transform to convert between world and skull-local space so I can place each primitive correctly using rotation and position offsets.

Now I'm sketching the actual skull geometry: a scaled sphere for the cranium, flattened capsules for brow ridges, and sweeping horn paths curving backward and outward from the posterior skull with tapering radii, while checking that the horns and cheek spikes don't collide with the haft or blade root.

Blade stays clear at that point, so the horns can sweep outward elegantly without collision. Now I'm sketching the snout as a loft from the cranium forward, defining stations for the upper jaw with widths and heights tapering along its length.

Adding the nose bump, nostrils, and rows of conical upper teeth with two larger fangs, then the lower jaw as a hinged bone that opens via pose rotation, with its own teeth cones pointing up. I'm placing a floating teal soul orb just in front of the open mouth, cradled between the jaws.

Now I'm designing the eyes as glowing teal sockets with dark bases and bright inner spheres, plus side frills as fan-shaped extruded plates with spiked edges, possibly with glowing membrane panels.

Then I'm adding a gold brow crown with a teal forehead gem, and laying out the neck vertebrae geometry as spool-shaped lathed segments running from the collar up to the skull, with small bone-ridge fins along the spine for added detail.

I'm figuring out vertebra spacing and size tapering, plus a glowing teal marrow core visible through gaps between segments, and considering replacing the mid-grip vertebrae with a leather-and-gold-wire wrap instead.

For the grip wrap, I'm using a spiral stripe pattern based on angle around the axis combined with vertical position, alternating dark purple and gold, with gold ring collars capping each end. Then I'm dividing the spine into three zones: lower shaft as bone, grip as wrapped, and upper shaft as bone again with some glow.

For the pommel, I'm sculpting a dragon-claw foot with three curved talon sweeps gripping the plinth, tapering from thicker at the ferrule to pointed tips, with small spheres at the knuckle joints and a lathed ferrule section banded in gold sitting atop a faint glowing socket ring where it meets the plinth.

For the soul orbit, I'm planning a ring of five small glowing low-poly orbs spiraling at varying heights around the haft near y=1.5, each trailing a flame-card wisp tail, tied to a single "soulRing" hinge joint to keep the joint count minimal.

For the ribbons, I'm adding two tattered violet-to-teal gradient membrane strips hanging about 0.6m from the collar below the blade root, gold-trimmed with slight catmull sway, but realizing they'd need to route around the skull sitting at y 1.9–2.1 since the collar attachment is at y=2.14.

I decide to hang them behind the haft instead, attached at the back (z=-0.06) and draping down to y 1.4 with a slight outward flow so they're visible from the side/back but partly hidden behind the haft from the front. I'm also adding a small chain charm off the counter-claw tip—gold dragon-scale links with a teal crystal teardrop—and a dark gold lathe collar ring with rivets clamping the blade root between two gold jaw plates.

I'm adding an ornate gold mount plate at the blade root with a teal gem centerpiece, then thinking through how to decorate the blade's dark band: painted rune dashes or chevron notches along the local x-coordinate, plus a few glowing rune sigil decals placed as small textured planes along the curve of the band.

I'm working out the orientation and sizing of these rune decals — positioning them flat against the blade's front and back faces, keeping their width narrow relative to the dark band, and designing simple stroke-based rune shapes in a small SVG viewbox with gold/teal coloring, then confirming the correct face normal direction for placement.

For the ribs, I'm planning thin bone-like tubes running from the root fan out to the edge at several points along the blade, sitting slightly proud of the surface on both faces so they cross over the dark and teal bands, tapering in radius and kept narrow enough not to clutter the glow effect.

Now I'm thinking about the teal band's inner edge and whether to make it wavy or keep it smooth, and adding a row of seven outward-pointing dorsal spines along the outer curve that shrink in length as they approach the tip, rendered in bone color with shading.

I also want to run a thick hexagonal bone tube right along the outer edge at k=0.0 so the blade looks rimmed by a fat bone, with the spine band extruded starting at k=0.04, and the tip staying fixed where the inner curve ends.

Writing curve geometry code...

I need to dedupe the polygon points where the top and bottom rows meet at the tip, since both rows converge to the same point there, while keeping the band distinct everywhere width is nonzero. The tip gets marked as sharp, with the two rows meeting exactly at t=1.

For the root end, I'll close the outline with a straight segment between the row starts at t=0, and plan the extrusion thickness with a small bevel for the bands, layering overlapping extrudes without issue. For the dragon-scale textures I'll use small scale sizes with a bone-colored palette and dark edges, and for the soul wisp cards I'm sketching a teal flame shape with a gradient, cut at 0.5 alpha so only the color gradient shows through.

Now I'm working out the floor plinth rune ring as a flat SVG decal with concentric circles and glyph ticks, sized and textured so the strokes stay crisp at the target resolution, then building the plinth itself as a tiered low-poly cylinder stack in dark obsidian tones.

I'm sinking the plinth so its top disc sits right at the scythe butt, then adding corner detail—bone fang spikes jutting outward from each octagon vertex and small glowing teal gems inset at each face center.

I'm also clustering a few teal crystal shards near the back-left of the plinth top, keeping them inside the radius so they don't overlap the rune circle, then moving on to refine the skull details.

Before writing the full code, I want to set up helper functions to avoid repetition and double-check API details like how glow() expects a target and how b.cards returns an array of meshes. I'm also defining a bone color palette with light, mid, and dark tones to keep the material scheme consistent and within budget.

For accents I'm leaning toward a soul-cyan/teal glow paired with deep teal shadows and white-hot highlights, plus gold trim, with violet tones as a secondary base -- giving the eyes a bright teal glow that reads as magical.

Now I'm setting up the geometry: defining a tilted basis and origin point for placing haft segments, then building the collar ring at the blade root and gold clamp plates shaped like angular dragon-wing points around the haft.

Still defining blade geometry...

Adding ribbed gold bands with a teal glow stripe to the lower claw, then working out the skull mount position relative to the haft so the cranium and occiput sit correctly without the haft awkwardly poking through.

I'm pushing the skull forward slightly so the haft passes cleanly behind it, and adding a slight downward pitch (~10°) so the skull appears to look down, working out the rotation sign convention around the X axis to confirm positive angles tip the forward-facing bone downward consistently with the jaw pose rule.

I'm setting up a helper to apply translation plus axis-angle rotation to local coordinates, then starting to lay out the skull's geometric pieces—beginning with the cranium as a scaled, flat-shaded sphere positioned slightly up and centered.

Now I'm working through brow ridges as capsule shapes from forehead to mid-face, dark ellipsoid eye sockets embedded into the sides of the skull, and glowing eye orbs that protrude slightly outward from those sockets with a vertical slit detail.

For the snout I'm lofting through a series of stations with decreasing width and height as it tapers forward, and noting that unassigned parts need their bone explicitly set to the skull joint rather than defaulting to the nearest one.

Writing wrapper helper functions...

Now I'm sketching the joint hierarchy: a root base joint, a skull joint parented to it for the jaw, a soul ring joint higher up with hinge role, and possibly an orb joint near the skull for the floating soul orb in the mouth. I'm debating whether the ribbons need their own hinge joints for flutter or can stay static as simple membrane sweeps between chains.

Settling on rigid ribbon joints (ribbonA, ribbonB) hinged at the top, plus a small charm joint hanging on a hinge from the claw, bringing the total to around seven joints with roles like "head" and "jaw" defined for the skull and jaw connection.

Now I'm working out the teeth placement, computing tooth positions along the snout by interpolating the jaw's half-width at different z-depths so each tooth sits correctly inset from the edge.

Writing cone geometry for teeth...

For the lower jaw, I'm lofting a frustum shape through three stations near the hinge, tapering width and height toward the chin, then pitching the whole jaw 28° around the joint before anything else gets posed underneath it.

The orb floats independently in front of the open mouth, parented to the skull rather than the jaw so it stays fixed as the jaw rotates away. I'm positioning it around (0,-0.1,0.48) with a small radius, then wrapping it in tilted glowing torus rings to suggest a swirling energy effect.

I'll add a flame-like tongue inside the mouth too -- a thin glowing capsule running along the lower jaw, parented to the jaw bone so it follows the opening motion. Then the jaw pose rotation gets applied afterward so all jaw-attached geometry, including this tongue, lands correctly in the open position.

For the frill plates on the cheeks, I'm extruding a spiked fan outline in the local z-y plane with the thickness axis pointing along x so the plates face outward from the skull, positioning each one using the H3 anchor points scaled back from the head.

I'm layering a bone-dark underplate with finger spikes radiating from the root plus a smaller inner teal membrane panel offset for a glowing effect, then moving on to design the horns as swept tubes with ring bands along a curved local path.

I'm checking that horn placement doesn't visually clash with the blade root plate from the front view, so I'm shortening the horns and angling them outward-back to avoid overlap on the +X side.

Checking whether the horn tip at that outward position collides with the blade root's projected footprint, since the blade band at that same u value spans a y-range that could visually overlap.

The horn tip sits just below that inner edge, so the composition works -- a skull with wide swept horns nestled beneath the blade, with the haft reaching up to the same height. I'll place the skull mesh at those coordinates and move on to painting it: bone coloring with mottled texture and cracks across the cranium, using the shared paint sheet approach for consistency with other skull parts.

For the bone paint I want a countershading effect layered over mottled bone tones, so lighter highlights hit the top surfaces and darker shadows wrap the undersides, mimicking hand-painted highlights like in stylized game art. I'll apply the same painted treatment to the haft vertebrae, but I need to watch texel density -- with so many painted surfaces (blade bands, plinth, etc.) I should limit what actually gets painted detail versus flat color to keep things efficient.

For sizing, a 1024 atlas should be enough given the model's scale and painted area, giving roughly 3mm texel resolution, which is plenty.

Now I'm working out the ribbon membranes -- defining two converging edge paths so the strip tapers to a point at the tip rather than staying rectangular, giving it a tattered swallowtail look.

For color, I'm blending violet into teal toward the tip using a smoothstep gradient, with a gold trim painted along both edges where the across-coordinate nears 0 or 1.

I'm now laying out the actual 3D points for ribbon A, tracing it hanging from the haft and cascading down and back with a tapering width, then starting the offset edge B to build the mirrored strip.

For the second ribbon I'm giving it a slight twist and mirroring it with different lengths on the other side, hinged as its own joint, plus setting a default thickness for the membrane.

Now I'm working out a hanging charm from the lower claw tip -- converting the claw's blade coordinates into world position, then chaining small gold torus links down with alternating rotations to a teardrop soul-gem pendant at the end, all attached via its own hinge joint.

I'm also planning a soul orbit ring: five glowing icosahedron orbs spiraling around a joint above the hilt, each paired with an upward flame-card wisp using cross-facing cards so they read from any angle, plus a few drifting soul orbs near the blade's inner edge bound to a new "soulDrift" hinge joint rather than rigidly fixed.

Now I'm adding a gold filigree crown band sweeping across the skull's brow using a curved tube path, with a small glowing teal gem set at its center, while skipping the tassel idea on the haft's dragon-scale lashing and sticking with simpler ribbons instead.

I'm sketching the facial detail pass -- dark sphere nostrils, small bone ridge spikes along the snout, and cheek jugal spikes angled outward on each side -- while skipping the under-brow glow stripes to keep things cleaner. I'm also planning neural spines with a teal marrow rod along the haft's vertebrae and rune glyph decals on the blade before moving to actually write the code.

Now I'm computing the tube geometry sweeping along the blade's outer rim using sampled curve points, then adding dorsal spikes along that outer edge whose direction and length vary with position -- taller near the base, tapering toward the tip, each oriented outward using the local tangent and normal of the curve.

I'm leaving the inner cutting edge smooth without spikes, and instead adding glowing teal flame-wisp cards along it, anchored at points on the inner edge and oriented to trail backward toward the root, giving a flowing flame-trail effect off the blade.

I'll add a second card at 90° with cross: true so the wisp flames stay visible from all sides, using lean 0 and bend 0 for teal glow flames tapering up and drifting off the blade's edge, with the facing axis set to the inner normal pointing away from the blade.

Now I'm designing the wisp flame shape as a tall SVG with an S-curved tapered body in teal with a lighter inner core, plus three alternating gold/teal rune textures drawn on small square planes, and planning the texture atlas with wisp, rune, and plinth textures loaded together.

For readability from above I want a large glowing teal sigil decal on the plinth ring, positioned relative to the plinth's radius. I'm starting to set up imports for geometry builders, paint/texture helpers, and math utilities, while thinking through how to type point arrays as tuples versus plain arrays.

Now I'm figuring out vertebra geometry — using lathe profiles to spin a spool shape per vertebra, merging vertebra geometries by color so paints apply correctly via UVs, keeping the marrow rod as a separate piece. Defining lathe profile points...

Working out normal directions for each path segment...

Now I need to merge all vertebra geometries with consistent flat shading, plus add transverse processes as small cones and a dorsal spine, combining everything into single bone-colored merged geometries.

I'm planning each vertebra with a tapering radius, writing a function that builds the merged lathe geometry for a given height and scale factor. For the grip section, I'm sketching a core rod with a spiral paint pattern instead of individual vertebra segments.

Still writing wrap logic...

I'm also planning gold collar rings at specific heights along the shaft, plus a lathe profile for the bottom ferrule.

For the glowing core, I'm sweeping a thin teal rod up the center that peeks through small gaps between the vertebra segments, tuning the gap size so the glow is visible but subtle in the grip zone.

So the rod pokes through at the waist, creating a glowing band effect between the flared ends - like a luminous ring. Now I need to figure out the teal soul glow and ferrule details, then start structuring the code into a single file.

Thinking through the cards signature now - frames take a position and direction, and glow wraps around parts or sweeps. For texture decals on blades, I need to set up the plane orientation so dir points along the face normal and up aligns with the blade's Y-axis, making sure runes read correctly even from the back face.

Now I'm working out rune placement along the dark band of the blade: picking center and spacing points, checking the band width against rune size so they fit without crowding near the tip. I'm also laying out the k-parameter zones along the spine—bone band, dark band, teal glow, and white-hot tip—to figure out where ribs and the rim tube should sit.

The teal band is the brightest, most saturated zone, so I'm considering splitting it into stepped tones (deep teal, bright teal, white) for a cel-shaded look instead of a smooth gradient, and planning the stepped extrusion thickness for each band to create a beveled, layered blade profile.

I'm now working out where the inner ribs should sit relative to each layer's surface height so they hug the blade's contour rather than floating above thinner layers — using a piecewise z-offset based on each band's thickness, accepting the stair-step jumps along the rib sweep as an acceptable tradeoff for now.

Now I'm moving on to writing the skull helper functions, starting with the pitch constant.

I'm defining a head center point and small rotation helpers that apply a pitch rotation around an axis before converting to coordinate arrays, watching for a possible type mismatch between `number[]` and expected tuple types that I may need to cast explicitly.

Now I'm setting up the plinth geometry using a cylinder helper that builds tapered cylinders with top/bottom radii, height, and segment count, positioning each piece vertically with flat shading.

For the tiered design, I'm planning three stacked rings: a dark violet mottled stone tier, a gold band, another stone tier, topped off around 0.14 with a glowing rune decal, plus teal inlay slits on the lowest tier's faces.

Working out the octagon geometry now — placing each inlay box at the correct face center by rotating around Y so face angles land at 22.5° increments, keeping the local +Z axis aligned with each face's outward direction.

Then I'm positioning bone-colored spike fangs at the vertices (at 22.5°+45k offsets), angling them up and outward like dragon claws from the top of the first tier, while checking the base radius stays clear of the second tier underneath.

Now I'm figuring out where to cluster crystals on the plinth ledges — mapping out the shrinking tier radii (T1 shelf around .56-.64, T2 shelf around .5-.56) to find spots outside the rune circle on the gold-banded ledges.

Placing small hex-prism crystal clusters at four positions between the fangs on the T1 shelf, varying heights and tilts for a teal glow, built from stacked cylinder-and-cone geometry. Now I'm working out the butt claws — three curved claws at 90°, 210°, and 330° sweeping outward from the ferrule using a polar path.

I'm adding a small gold ring with a teal glow disc around the ferrule base, plus collar bands and rivets, then planning the gold paint shading pattern for the final detail pass.

Now I'm writing the blade geometry logic: generating outer and inner curve paths, interpolating between them with a blend factor, and creating a band outline function that sweeps forward along one edge and back along the other to form a closed shape.

To avoid degenerate thin triangles near the tip, I'll stop the thin bands slightly before t=1 (around 0.985) rather than letting them collapse at the exact tip point.

Now I'm handling the extrude direction setup, deduplicating adjacent near-identical outline points, and sketching out the claw sweeps and rib geometry using bezier curves from root to inner points.

Rib roots should be tucked under the clamp plate so knuckle spheres stay hidden, and ribs can start close to the hilt there. For the soul flame cards along the inner edge, I'm placing twelve frames spaced along the blade, each oriented to face outward from the inner side using a normal computed from the direction between inner and outer edges.

Now I'm adding an orb assembly near the hilt — a glowing teal sphere shell with a smaller white glowing core, surrounded by two tilted torus rings (one teal, one gold) for a layered mystical look.

I'm placing six randomly-oriented flame cards around the orb's surface so they appear to flicker outward, parenting the whole orb to a hinge joint so it can spin independently, and setting up a separate ring joint for floating wisp elements. Now I'm starting the SVG markup for the wisp shape itself.

Still writing wisp SVG paths...

Still writing plinth ring SVG...

For the ribbon membranes, I need hinge joints attached to the base bone, with the root joint positioned at the top and oriented upward. Now I'm figuring out the loft parameters for things like skull teeth, defining stations with width/height arrays to sweep each bone segment.

Working out jaw lofts, brow capsules, and dark eye sockets with pitch-rotated spheres... then setting up teeth placement along the jaw by spacing them at intervals and computing the half-width at each position.

Still placing teeth...

input.command: cd ~/tmp-archive/sonnet-100/soulScytheSonnet/ && sed -n 1,60p src/frame.ts | head -80 && grep -n "export" src/math.ts | head -20 && grep -n "export function countershade" -A6 src/paint.ts
